articles.expand: Reuters reports, citing EU diplomats, that EU leaders are set to sign off on Pablo Hernández de Cos as the next president of the European Central Bank. This has been well telegraphed. Christine Lagarde is leaving early. She steps down on February 7, nine months before her eight-year term was due to end in October 2027. The timing is political. Leaving early lets EU leaders lock in a successor before April's French presidential election, where polls favour Marine Le Pen (and will be a major event in FX markets next year).
